android_fork_merge.status: Ready for review (port compiles on arm64)
android_fork_merge.notes: Deep sync of the fork with upstream horizon-rust/horizon:main as of 2026-11-15. The fork keeps: Compose/JNI launcher, ARM64 Rust build with the Android touch stack, .hmod/.hnmod native-mod pipeline, Android renderer preparation machinery (deferred background renderer build, recreate_surface on resume, GL-blocking guards), per-instance presets, and the Android workflows. Upstream's crate split (horizon-client-lib, horizon-hooks, horizon-official, horizon-optifine, etc.) and NATIVE_HOOKS_API 645 are adopted. Gameplay now lives in the library, so JNI/activity code stays in horizon-android and the library reaches the platform through a host table it installs once (crates/horizon-client/src/android_host.rs; device_runtime::Frame records the frame on drop). The launcher files the bridge shares are compiled through launcher/src/android_shared.rs (the launcher needs GPUI, so it cannot be a crate dependency); their backend resolves game paths to the app home on Android. Upstream stopped running WebAssembly code mods, so the fork's mod-menu runtime hooks are documented no-ops; the .hnmod native-mod path is unchanged. Native Android checks build arm64 only (.github/workflows/android-source.yml and packaging/android/source-checks.yml stay byte-identical). Deployment workflows remain disabled under .github/upstream-workflows/.

base_selection: Merge base from git merge upstream/main (17,923 upstream commits since 2026-11-01 nightly)
review: Port completed 2026-11-15 on sync/horizon-main-2026-11-14 (two-parent merge 6005c64b0d, upstream b396fcfe01, base 8c02c0b853). `cargo check -p horizon-android` (aarch64 Android host, single job, no debuginfo) runs clean locally; the 17 Python Android tests pass; tools/check_public_tree.py passes; the two Android CI workflow copies are identical. Conflicts were resolved by taking upstream unless the fork's Android glue was the behavior; the missing upstream NEEDS_PORT/needs_port registry rules were restored after the merge had dropped them. CI on the sync branch (android-source arm64, android-dev fast APK arm64) is the remaining gate; no on-device behavior is claimed beyond what that CI verifies.
